sentences.en: Okay, now back to today's episode.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在回到今天的节目。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Last week, President Trump hit several countries with yet another round of punishing tariffs.
sentences.zh: 上周，特朗普总统对好几个国家实施了又一轮严厉的关税。

sentences.en: So far, the economy's been resilient in the face of his trade war.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，面对他的贸易战，经济表现出了韧性。

sentences.en: But it's unclear how long that'll laSt.
sentences.zh: 但目前还不清楚这种情况能持续多久。

sentences.en: Today, I talked to my colleague, Dealbook editor Andrew Ross Sorkin, about what CEOs are telling him privately about Trump's tariffs and where they think all of this is headed.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了我的同事、Dealbook编辑安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金，聊聊首席执行官们私下对特朗普关税的看法，以及他们认为这一切将走向何方。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月11日，星期一。

sentences.en: Andrew, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We are coming to you because you are one of the most deeply sourced and best connected business reporters out there.
sentences.zh: 我们来找你是因为你是业内消息最灵通、人脉最广的商业记者之一。

sentences.en: You literally talked to the president on CNBC last week.
sentences.zh: 上周你甚至在CNBC上直接采访了总统。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我采访了。

sentences.en: It was kind of wild.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点疯狂。

sentences.en: Kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 有点不可思议。

sentences.en: And you're regularly talking to business executives who've been navigating these ups and downs of tariffs for months.
sentences.zh: 而且你经常与那些几个月来一直在应对这些关税起伏的企业高管交流。

sentences.en: I feel like by this point, we've asked this question on the show over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我觉得到目前为止，我们在节目里已经反复问过这个问题了。

sentences.en: But help me make sense of this moment.
sentences.zh: 但请帮我理清目前的局势。

sentences.en: What is the status of Trump's tariffs as of right now?
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，特朗普的关税现状如何？

sentences.en: So the big shift is that after many, many months of speculation about tariffs, about what the
sentences.zh: 所以最大的转变是，在经历了长达数月关于关税的种种猜测之后——

sentences.en: ultimate rates would look like, about how severe they would be, and how businesses would have to navigate them, that the tariffs are actually here.
sentences.zh: 关于最终的税率会是多少、会有多严厉，以及企业该如何应对——关税现在真的来了。

sentences.en: So we had what the president called Liberation Day back in April.
sentences.zh: 所以在4月份的时候，我们经历了总统所说的“解放日”。

sentences.en: He announced these remarkably high tariffs.
sentences.zh: 他宣布了这些高得惊人的关税。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking about numbers in excess of 100 percent, in some cases, 145 percent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们讨论的数字超过了100%，在某些情况下甚至达到了145%。

sentences.en: And business leaders, politicians around the world had a collective freakout.
sentences.zh: 全球的商界领袖和政客们都集体慌了神。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But over the last several months, those tariff rates continually got delayed and postponed.
sentences.zh: 但在过去的几个月里，这些关税税率一再被延迟和推迟。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We got that taco meme on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 华尔街甚至出现了那个“懦夫”梗。

sentences.en: The taco meme.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个“懦夫”梗。

sentences.en: Trump always chickens out.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总是临阵退缩。

sentences.en: Trump always chickens out.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总是临阵退缩。

sentences.en: And so here we are in the month of August, and we now have, in large part, a framework for what the tariff rates are going to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在来到了8月份，在很大程度上，我们终于有了一个关于关税税率的框架。

sentences.en: President Trump's sweeping global tariffs for more than 90 countries have come into effect.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统针对90多个国家的全面全球关税已经正式生效。

sentences.en: Including Japan, the U.K., and the European Union.
sentences.zh: 包括日本、英国和欧盟。

sentences.en: And the president, to some degree, at least isn't totally chickening out.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，总统至少没有完全临阵退缩。

sentences.en: We're saying this is probably the biggest deal ever reached in any capacity, trade or beyond trade.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这可能是任何领域（无论是贸易还是贸易之外）达成的最大协议。

sentences.en: And now, if you are a U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你是一家美国公司

sentences.en: company that is importing goods into the United States, you are writing a check to Uncle Sam.
sentences.zh: 正在向美国进口货物，你就是在给山姆大叔开支票。

sentences.en: We have hundreds of billions of dollars pouring into our country now.
sentences.zh: 现在有数千亿美元正涌入我们国家。

sentences.en: We should have done this many years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们早就该这么做了。

sentences.en: So what are some of the rates that we're now looking at actually amount to?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在看到的实际税率大概是多少？

sentences.en: So if goods are coming in from the EU, you're paying 15 percent.
sentences.zh: 如果货物来自欧盟，你要支付15%的关税。

sentences.en: If goods are coming in from Japan, you're paying 15 percent.
sentences.zh: 如果货物来自日本，你要支付15%的关税。

sentences.en: If goods are coming in from China right this moment, you're paying actually only 30 percent with the prospect that you could be paying 125 percent because that piece of the puzzle
sentences.zh: 如果此时此刻货物来自中国，你实际上只需要支付30%的关税，不过未来可能要支付125%，因为拼图的这一部分

sentences.en: has not been fit into the puzzle just yet.
sentences.zh: 还没完全拼好。

sentences.en: Still unsettled.
sentences.zh: 尚未敲定。

sentences.en: Still unsettled.
sentences.zh: 尚未敲定。

sentences.en: By the way, India unsettled.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，印度也没有敲定。

sentences.en: 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 百分之五十。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What was that, Andrew?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，那是什么？

sentences.en: That shocking rate on India that was just announced of 50 percent really took me by surprise.
sentences.zh: 刚刚宣布的对印度高达50%的惊人税率确实让我大吃一惊。

sentences.en: I think it took a lot of people by surprise.
sentences.zh: 我想这也让很多人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Well, it's a huge about face for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对美国政府以及我们国家与印度的关系来说是一个巨大的180度大转弯。

sentences.en: government and our country's relationship with India.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，我们实际上一直在试图推动许多公司撤出中国等地，将制造业转移到印度等地。

sentences.en: For the last several years, we have been trying to actually push a lot of companies to actually get out of places like China and move their manufacturing to places like India.
sentences.zh: 但在过去的几年里，我们实际上一直在试图推动许多公司撤出中国等地，将制造业转移到印度等地。

sentences.en: But India has been one of the biggest importer of oil from Russia.
sentences.zh: 但印度一直是俄罗斯石油的最大进口国之一。

sentences.en: And so they have been effectively propping up the Russian economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们实际上一直在支撑俄罗斯经济。

sentences.en: And Trump is now saying that he's going to use the tariff chess piece, if you will, to change that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普现在表示，他要利用关税这枚棋子来改变这种动态。

sentences.en: OK, so we have these huge tariffs on India.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我们对印度征收了如此巨额的关税。

sentences.en: We have different rates all over the world, a sense that these things are really in effect.
sentences.zh: 我们在世界各地有不同的税率，让人感觉到这些关税真的生效了。

sentences.en: How are all the CEOs, all the executives, the investors, the policymakers that you talk to reacting?
sentences.zh: 你所接触到的所有首席执行官、高管、投资者和政策制定者对此有何反应？

sentences.en: Honestly, the surprising thing is, at this point, they're actually a lot calmer about it all than you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 老实说，令人惊讶的是，到了这个地步，他们其实比你想象的要冷静得多。

sentences.en: They may not like it, but I think they're recognizing and deciding that this is their new normal.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不喜欢这样，但我认为他们正在认识到并决定，这就是他们的新常态。

sentences.en: And the other thing that's so surprising is just how sanguine the markets and the investor class has been around this.
sentences.zh: 另一个令人惊讶的是，市场和投资阶层对此表现得如此泰然处夫。

sentences.en: Because, you know, back in April, there really was a freak out, not just among the CEOs, but
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，早在4月份时，确实引发了一场恐慌，不仅在CEO中间，

sentences.en: the stock market fell precipitously until the president delayed and postponed these tariffs.
sentences.zh: 股市也急剧下跌，直到总统延迟和推迟了这些关税。

sentences.en: Yep, I remember that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得那一幕。

sentences.en: You know, now in recent days, you've had the market either flat or actually go up, which suggests that the market is settling in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在这几天，市场要么持平，要么实际上还在上涨，这表明市场正在适应。

sentences.en: And to some degree, they're saying this is OK.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他们觉得这还可以接受。

sentences.en: OK, just explain that to me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，请向我解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: There's a state of permanence now about these tariffs.
sentences.zh: 现在这些关税呈现出了一种永久的状态。

sentences.en: One way or the other, for at least the next several years, if not the next decades, and
sentences.zh: 无论如何，至少在未来几年，甚至未来几十年里——

sentences.en: I say decades plural, I think there's a recognition that we are going to be living with some form of tariff.
sentences.zh: 我这里用的是复数“几十年”——我认为大家已经认识到，我们将长期生活在某种形式的关税之中。

sentences.en: And by the way, maybe those tariffs will change and go up and down.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，也许这些关税会改变，会忽高忽低。

sentences.en: But there's now a sense that it's here.
sentences.zh: 但现在有一种感觉，那就是它已经扎根了。

sentences.en: There's a window into what that actually looks like, somewhere between 10% on the lowest end and maybe 30% on the highest end.
sentences.zh: 大家对它到底是个什么样子有了个窗口期的了解，大概在最低10%到最高30%之间。

sentences.en: And so they're starting to realize we're just going to have to plan to live with this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始意识到，我们只能做好准备接受并适应这一切。

sentences.en: Now, I don't want to overstate the sense that everybody's cool with this, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我不想夸大那种“每个人都对此无所谓”的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: Inside the boardrooms and the corner offices of corporate America, they're worried.
sentences.zh: 在企业界的董事会和高管办公室里，大家还是很焦虑的。

sentences.en: They're just saying, OK, we're going to have to figure out how to deal with our worry.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在说，好吧，我们得想办法应对这种焦虑。

sentences.en: And that's different than the last couple of months of, OK, we're worried, we're freaked out, and we think that somehow if we can just get to the president, we're going to somehow
sentences.zh: 这和过去几个月的情况不同，当时大家都在想，好吧，我们很担心，我们很恐慌，我们觉得只要能联系到总统，我们就能设法

sentences.en: get him to back off all of this.
sentences.zh: 让他收回这一切。

sentences.en: And now that they've realized that that's not the case, they're like, OK, we have to actually just figure out what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们意识到事实并非如此，于是他们觉得，好吧，我们必须真正开始想办法解决它了。

sentences.en: Can we get into that?
sentences.zh: 我们能深入谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Actually, up until now, how have CEOs navigated these tariffs?
sentences.zh: 事实上，在此之前，首席执行官们是如何应对这些关税的？

sentences.en: I mean, I can imagine it's been a really rough road.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以想象这一定是一条非常艰难的路。

sentences.en: I think there's two things that have been going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去一段时间主要发生了两件事。

sentences.en: One is they've been making pilgrimages to Washington to see lawmakers, to try to see the president, to try to see all of his deputies and lieutenants around him and desperately
sentences.zh: 一是他们一直在组团去华盛顿拜访议员，试图见总统，试图见他周围的所有副手和心腹，拼命地

sentences.en: try to persuade them away from this, clearly unsuccessfully.
sentences.zh: 试图劝说他们放弃这个念头，显然没有成功。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然没有。

sentences.en: The other thing they've been doing is spending an extraordinary amount of time trying to rethink their supply chain.
sentences.zh: 另一件他们一直在做的事，是花大量时间试图重新构思他们的供应链。

sentences.en: Can they move goods from one place to the other?
sentences.zh: 他们能不能把货物从一个地方转移到另一个地方？

sentences.en: In certain cases, they were trying to get as much of their supplies into the United States early to try to get ahead of the tariffs.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们试图尽早将尽可能多的物资运进美国，以此来赶在关税生效前囤货。

sentences.en: So you had Ford, for example, literally sending trucks back and forth between the border of Mexico and the U.S., bringing as many supplies to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，福特汽车曾字面意义上派卡车在墨西哥和美国边境来回穿梭，尽可能多地将物资运往美国

sentences.en: as they could because they knew they're going to slap us with these tariffs.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道对方会把这些关税狠狠砸向他们。

sentences.en: Okay, so they're desperately trying to get the Trump team to back off.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们拼命想让特朗普团队退缩。

sentences.en: That doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 这行不通。

sentences.en: They've been trying to stockpile to avoid the hit of tariffs.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在囤积物资以避开关税的打击。

sentences.en: In the meantime, they haven't been raising prices.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们一直没有提价。

sentences.en: That's been a big mystery.
sentences.zh: 这一直是个巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: What's going on there?
sentences.zh: 那里的情况到底是怎样的？

sentences.en: Why haven't they passed on the cost of these tariffs to consumers?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们没有把这些关税的成本转嫁给消费者？

sentences.en: So first of all, just mea culpa myself, which is I think I, like a lot of people, thought in April that we were going to see higher prices and higher prices super quickly.
sentences.zh: 首先，我得做个自我检讨，我觉得我和许多人一样，在4月份时以为我们会看到物价上涨，而且物价会飞速上涨。

sentences.en: I love that you're admitting this.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你勇于承认这一点。

sentences.en: Well, look, when you saw the president out with, in some cases, tariffs that were supposed to be implemented overnight at 145 percent, you would invariably say, if in fact that's
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，当你看到总统亮出的那些在某些情况下本应在一夜之间实施的145%的关税时，你不可避免地会想，如果事实确

sentences.en: true, prices should go up.
sentences.zh: 实如此，物价就应该上涨。

sentences.en: So the first piece that I was just wrong about was actually that these things would get delayed and postponed.
sentences.zh: 所以，我第一个判断失误的地方在于，我没想到这些关税会被延迟和推迟。

sentences.en: The other thing, though, when you talk to CEOs of some of the big retail companies and just any major manufacturer here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 不过，另一方面，当你与一些大型零售公司的首席执行官以及美国任何一家主要制造商交谈时

sentences.en: is they say that they've been trying to eat as much of the tariff costs so far as they can.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，到目前为止，他们一直在尽最大努力自己消化这些关税成本。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: It's interesting because if you go back to the pandemic, companies did something called taking a price very quickly.
sentences.zh: 很有意思的是，如果你回想一下疫情期间，各家公司做了一件叫做迅速提价的事。

sentences.en: They were very worried about inflation and they would almost raise prices even before they got hit with the costs themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们非常担心通货膨胀，甚至在自己承担成本之前就已经开始提高价格了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so I thought, and I think a lot of people thought, OK, even before the tariffs are here, companies are just going to raise the prices because they want to get ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，而且很多人也以为，好吧，甚至在关税到来之前，企业就会直接提高价格，因为他们想占领先机。

sentences.en: They're going to repeat their pandemic playbook.
sentences.zh: 他们会重复他们在疫情时的那套做法。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Two things have come into play that are different.
sentences.zh: 但现在有两个不同的新因素在起作用。

sentences.en: One is that the economy is not as strong as it was during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 一是经济不像疫情期间那么强劲。

sentences.en: And so there was a real concern that actually the market can't really accept a much higher price at the kind of volume that some of these companies are selling their products at,
sentences.zh: 因此人们真的很担心，在其中一些公司销售产品的这种体量下，市场其实无法接受高得多的价格，

sentences.en: that if you were the first mover to raise prices, you would actually lose market share.
sentences.zh: 如果你是第一个带头涨价的人，你实际上会失去市场份额。

sentences.en: Basically, if you're the first one to raise your prices, if you're a Walmart, your customers might turn to a target.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你是第一个涨价的，如果你是沃尔玛，你的客户可能会转向塔吉特。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the other thing, and this is more anecdotal, is a sense among business leaders that given the president's propensity to critique them directly, if not more than that, that just
sentences.zh: 另一个情况，这更多是轶事层面的，是商界领袖的一种普遍感觉，鉴于总统倾向于直接批评他们，甚至更进一步，仅仅是

sentences.en: the optics of raising prices could cause the president to come out publicly and single them out.
sentences.zh: 涨价的外在观感就可能导致总统公开出来点名批评他们。

sentences.en: You saw this happen earlier this year already when there was a news report that Amazon was considering putting literally on the website the cost of the tariffs.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候你已经看到过这种情况了，当时有新闻报道称亚马逊正考虑把关税成本直接标在网站上。

sentences.en: The day that happened, the president was out there an hour or two later after that report, which was erroneous, by the way.
sentences.zh: 就在那天，报道出来的一两小时后，总统就公开发声了，顺便说一句，那篇报道是错误的。

sentences.en: But he was out there criticizing Amazon and Jeff Bezos was on the phone with the president.
sentences.zh: 但他还是出来批评了亚马逊，杰夫·贝佐斯当时正跟总统通电话。

sentences.en: Okay, and this may seem obvious, but just slow down here for me a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这听起来可能显而易见，但请你稍微放慢一点节奏。

sentences.en: Explain what the CEOs are so afraid of.
sentences.zh: 解释一下首席执行官们到底在怕什么。

sentences.en: I mean, what is it that they actually think will happen once the president gets so angry with them?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一旦总统对他们如此愤怒，他们到底认为会发生什么？

sentences.en: Look, I think this president has taken to targeting certain industries, certain companies that he doesn't like, for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为这位总统开始针对某些他不喜欢特定行业、特定公司，不管出于什么原因。

sentences.en: We saw his approach to universities in America.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了他对待美国高校的方式。

sentences.en: We saw him go after some of the big law firms in America.
sentences.zh: 我们看到他针对美国的一些大型律师事务所。

sentences.en: We saw him go after Paramount and CBS News, for example, and not allow a merger to take place until a settlement was reached.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们看到他针对派拉蒙和哥伦比亚广播公司新闻部，在达成和解之前不允许进行合并。

sentences.en: So I think that there's enough examples that the business community looks at and goes, it's not just that he's going to write something on Truth Social.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为商界看到了足够多的例子，他们觉得，这不仅仅是他在“真相社交”上写点东西那么简单。

sentences.en: If he wants to send his regulatory apparatus after us in one way or another, he can and he will.
sentences.zh: 如果他想以这样或那样的方式派监管机构来对付我们，他能做到，也一定会这么做。

sentences.en: And that's, I think, to some degree, just a deterrent for the entire business world when it comes to doing anything that they think would cause his wrath.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在某种程度上，对于整个商界来说，只要涉及任何他们认为会招致他愤怒的事情，这本身就是一种威慑。

sentences.en: So based on those private conversations that you're having, if you can share some of the learnings that you've had, how does that fear operate within a company?
sentences.zh: 那么根据你进行的这些私下对话，如果你能分享一些你所了解到的情况，这种恐惧在公司内部是如何运作的？

sentences.en: How does it change your decision making?
sentences.zh: 它如何改变你们的决策？

sentences.en: I'll give you a very tangible example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举一个非常具体的例子。

sentences.en: I talked to an executive at a company that was thinking of hiring somebody that had worked in the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 我跟一家公司的某位高管聊过，该公司当时正考虑雇佣一个曾在拜登政府工作过的人。

sentences.en: Not a particularly famous person in the Biden administration, but somebody who had worked in that Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 在拜登政府里并不是什么特别出名的人，但确实是一个曾在那个拜登政府工作过的人。

sentences.en: As part of thinking about whether to hire that person or not, they decided to make phone calls to back channel with people in and around the president to try to understand whether
sentences.zh: 作为是否雇佣这名员工的考量一部分，他们决定给总统身边的各种人士打电话进行私下沟通，试图了解

sentences.en: this person would be, quote unquote, acceptable to the president.
sentences.zh: 这个人是否能被总统“所接受”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Running individual hiring decisions by them.
sentences.zh: 连个别招聘决定都要跑去征求他们的意见。

sentences.en: I think that is the fear that he has imposed on parts of the business community.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是他给部分商界强加的恐惧。

sentences.en: And so you can look at that example.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看看那个例子。

sentences.en: That's a small example.
sentences.zh: 那只是个小例子。

sentences.en: Think about a company that's going to very publicly raise their prices.
sentences.zh: 想想一家准备公开大幅涨价的公司。

sentences.en: Well, if they can try to avoid raising their prices for as long as they can, they will.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他们能尽量避免涨价，能拖多久就拖多久，他们就会这么做。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting because I spent a lot of time talking to these leaders of companies, many of whom happen to be billionaires.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为我花了很多时间与这些公司的高管交谈，其中许多人恰好都是亿万富翁。

sentences.en: And you'd think, OK, they have this extraordinary amount of money.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，好吧，他们有这么多的钱。

sentences.en: They shouldn't be worried about the president or anybody else.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该担心总统或其他人。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's sort of the conventional wisdom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这算是某种传统智慧。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly why I asked the question.
sentences.zh: 对，这正是我问这个问题的原因。

sentences.en: But the truth is that I think almost singularly, this is the one person in the world who has more power than they do.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，几乎可以肯定是，这是世界上唯一一个拥有比他们更大权力的人。

sentences.en: But, you know, in fairness, CEOs have always been trying to stay in the good graces of, frankly, every president.
sentences.zh: 但是，说句公道话，首席执行官们一直都在试图赢得每一位总统的青睐。

sentences.en: And I was just with a tech CEO who actually made this point.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还跟一位科技公司CEO在一起，他实际上就提出了这一点。

sentences.en: He's a Trump supporter who said, look, during the Biden administration, you know, we were implementing all sorts of DEI and ESG-related programs in our companies to hopefully buy
sentences.zh: 他是一位特朗普的支持者，他说，听着，在拜登政府期间，你知道，我们在公司里实施了各种DEI（多元、公平、包容）和ESG（环境、社会和公司治理）相关的项目，希望能换取

sentences.en: some goodwill with the president.
sentences.zh: 对总统的一些好感。

sentences.en: We were investing in Evs.
sentences.zh: 我们在投资电动汽车。

sentences.en: Sometimes the Biden administration during COVID was requesting certain social media companies to take down certain posts, to amplify other things.
sentences.zh: 有时拜登政府在疫情期间会要求某些社交媒体公司删除某些帖子，推广其他内容。

sentences.en: And that some of the big tech companies were doing that, in part, to stay in the good graces of the administration that was ultimately regulating them in all sorts of other ways.
sentences.zh: 一些大型科技公司之所以照做，部分原因也是为了保持对他们进行全方位监管的政府的青睐。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not saying that those are all equivalent things.
sentences.zh: 现在，我并不是说这些都是一回事。

sentences.en: But I think it's just worth putting on the table.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这很值得摆上台面来说。

sentences.en: I get that what companies have been doing to adapt to tariffs is a way of kind of avoiding a conflict with the president.
sentences.zh: 我明白公司为适应关税一直在做的事情，是一种避免与总统发生冲突的方式。

sentences.en: But in this case, these companies, I mean, they have shareholders.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，这些公司，我的意思是，他们有股东。

sentences.en: They have to put out earnings reports, you know, and eating the cost of these tariffs just doesn't seem like a sustainable long-term solution.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们必须发布财报，而自己默默消化这些关税成本似乎并不是一个可持续的长期解决方案。

sentences.en: It isn't.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: And I think the more that I talk to some of these executives, especially in the last couple of weeks, there's a greater sense that things are about to change.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我跟其中一些高管交谈得越多，特别是在过去几周里，大家越发强烈地感觉到事情即将发生变化。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连连看》（Connections）游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是山姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天创作《拼字蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《字母箱》（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（chromesthesia）的病症。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com斜杠games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Okay, Andrew, you said this strategy is going to have to change.
sentences.zh: 好的，安德鲁，你说这个策略不得不改变。

sentences.en: What are you hearing about what CEOs are going to do?
sentences.zh: 你听到关于首席执行官们下一步要做什么的风声了吗？

sentences.en: You know, I just got back from Aspen, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我刚从科罗拉多州阿斯彭回来。

sentences.en: The Aspen Institute has something called the Aspen Economic Strategy Group meeting every year with many of the former Treasury secretaries in the United States, Hank Paulson,
sentences.zh: 阿斯彭研究所每年都会举行名为“阿斯彭经济战略小组”的会议，有许多美国前财政部长参加，如亨利·保尔森、

sentences.en: Larry Summers, and Janet Yellen, and so many CEOs, Larry Fink, who runs BlackRock, and Brian Moynihan, who runs Bank of America.
sentences.zh: 拉里·萨默斯和珍妮特·耶伦，还有很多首席执行官，比如掌管贝莱德的拉里·芬克和掌管美国银行的布赖恩·莫伊尼汉。

sentences.en: And one of the things just coming out of that meeting that you realize is that this is unsustainable, that at some point, the dam does have to break when it comes to prices.
sentences.zh: 从那次会议中得出的一个认识是，这种状态是不可持续的，在某个时候，在价格问题上，大坝确实必须要决堤了。

sentences.en: And so I think you're going to start to see prices rise.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你将开始看到价格上涨。

sentences.en: And there have been very public indicators of that already.
sentences.zh: 而且这方面已经出现了很多公开的迹象。

sentences.en: Amazon's said that they're going to have to raise prices, and they're going to have to raise prices for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊已经表示他们将不得不涨价，而且他们不得不涨价的原因有两个。

sentences.en: One is that their own suppliers are charging them more.
sentences.zh: 一是他们自己的供应商在向他们收取更高费用。

sentences.en: And also all of the sellers in their marketplace are going to be raising their prices because they, too, can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 同时，他们平台上的所有卖家也都会提高价格，因为他们同样承担不起。

sentences.en: This is an interesting example because Amazon was this company that was shamed by Trump,
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的例子，因为亚马逊曾是一家遭到特朗普羞辱的公司，

sentences.en: you know, didn't do this, backed away, and now they're saying, look, we're going to have to raise these prices.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没有这样做，选择了退缩，而现在他们却说，听着，我们不得不提高这些价格。

sentences.en: The rubber meets the road.
sentences.zh: 动真格的时候到了。

sentences.en: And while we're talking about the rubber meeting the road, another good example of this is Ford.
sentences.zh: 就在我们谈论动真格的时候，另一个很好的例子就是福特。

sentences.en: And I've spent time talking to Jim Farley, who's the CEO of Ford.
sentences.zh: 我花时间跟福特首席执行官吉姆·法利交谈过。

sentences.en: This is a company that he now says is going to lose $2 billion this year.
sentences.zh: 这家公司现在表示今年将亏损20亿美元。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so what I keep hearing over and over again from CEOs is that come this fall, they are going to be forced to raise their prices,
sentences.zh: 所以我从各位首席执行官那里不断听到的是，到了今年秋天，他们将被迫提高价格，

sentences.en: despite how much they'd like to keep them where they are if they could.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们多么希望能把价格维持在现状。

sentences.en: And what are they telling you about their hiring plans?
sentences.zh: 他们对你说了什么关于招聘计划的事吗？

sentences.en: Because we just got this pretty weak jobs report.
sentences.zh: 因为我们刚刚得到了这份相当疲软的就业报告。

sentences.en: Are your conversations with these executives reflecting any softening in the labor market?
sentences.zh: 你与这些高管的对话是否反映出劳动力市场有任何疲软迹象？

sentences.en: Well, you know, one of the things that a number of CEOs have told me just in the past couple of weeks is this idea that when they've had job openings,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，许多首席执行官在过去几周里告诉我的事情之一就是，当他们有职位空缺时，

sentences.en: that in many cases they're not filling them.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下他们并没有去填补。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons they're not filling them, and maybe that's reflective of what those job numbers suggest,
sentences.zh: 他们不填补的原因之一，也许这反映了这些就业数据所暗示的，

sentences.en: is this uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 就是这种不确定性。

sentences.en: The uncertainty of the tariffs have created an environment where they don't know what the future portends.
sentences.zh: 关税的不确定性创造了一个环境，让他们不知道未来会怎样。

sentences.en: They don't know once these tariffs are in effect and what prices they're going to ultimately have to sell their products at,
sentences.zh: 他们不知道一旦这些关税生效，他们最终得以什么价格出售产品，

sentences.en: what the business looks like in the same way that it did over the last six months.
sentences.zh: 业务是否还会像过去六个月那样。

sentences.en: But, you know, a lot of the data that we're getting still is inconclusive.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们得到的很多数据仍然没有定论。

sentences.en: If you look at, for example, Bank of America and their spending reports, they actually track every customer and how they use credit cards.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看美国银行及其消费报告，他们实际上追踪了每个客户以及他们如何使用信用卡。

sentences.en: They would say spending is up.
sentences.zh: 他们会说消费在上升。

sentences.en: You talk to the CEO of Uber, who I spoke to last week.
sentences.zh: 你跟优步的首席执行官谈谈，我上周和他聊过。

sentences.en: He would tell you there are more people that are ordering cars than before, that they're seeing no slowdown.
sentences.zh: 他会告诉你，叫车的人比以前更多了，他们没有看到任何放缓的迹象。

sentences.en: And so there is this sort of mixed picture, and I don't think we have real clarity just yet.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种有些复杂的景象，我认为我们现在还没有真正的清晰认识。

sentences.en: Okay, so we've talked about various ways that the companies might adapt to tariffs, these new potential strategies.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们讨论了公司适应关税的各种方式，这些潜在的新策略。

sentences.en: One, raising prices.
sentences.zh: 第一，涨价。

sentences.en: Another potential effect would be their hiring.
sentences.zh: 另一个潜在影响是他们的招聘。

sentences.en: What if they just did what the Trump administration wants them to do and moved manufacturing or sourcing to the United States?
sentences.zh: 如果他们只是按照特朗普政府希望的那样，将制造或采购转移到美国会怎么样？

sentences.en: I mean, that is a way of adapting to the tariffs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种适应关税的方式。

sentences.en: And many are looking at that.
sentences.zh: 许多人正在考虑这一点。

sentences.en: There is no question that they're trying, in some cases, to do that.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他们在某些情况下正在尝试这样做。

sentences.en: But it takes a very long time to be able to move supply chains around, be able to build a new manufacturing facility.
sentences.zh: 但要转移供应链、建立新的制造设施需要很长时间。

sentences.en: And so during that period of time, you still are going to have to import goods.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一时期，你仍然必须进口商品。

sentences.en: You know, an example of that is the way Apple is approaching all of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，苹果公司处理这一切的方式就是一个例子。

sentences.en: We just saw them announce that they are going to be investing an additional $100 billion in manufacturing here in America.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚看到他们宣布将额外投资1000亿美元在美国本土进行制造。

sentences.en: Huge announcement.
sentences.zh: 巨大的宣布。

sentences.en: But Tim Cook was asked in the White House, when would the actual iPhone, the full phone, be produced in the United States?
sentences.zh: 但蒂姆·库克在白宫被问及，真正的iPhone、完整的手机何时会在美国生产？

sentences.en: And he said not for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 他说短时间内不会。

sentences.en: And that's because even if he wanted to, just the physical nature of getting everything coordinated would take years.
sentences.zh: 这是因为即使他想这么做，光是协调一切的物理过程就需要数年时间。

sentences.en: So basically, even if the tariffs have the desired outcome, you could still see an economic impact in the meantime, while that is playing out.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，即使关税达到了预期的结果，在此期间，当这一切上演时，你仍然会看到经济受到影响。

sentences.en: The laws of economic gravity would suggest that at some point you have to pass the costs on to customers.
sentences.zh: 经济引力的规律表明，在某个时候你必须将成本转嫁给客户。

sentences.en: The question is, how big an impact that's going to have on the overall economy.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这会对整体经济产生多大的影响。

sentences.en: Given this picture that you've laid out for us with these cracks emerging in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你为我们描绘的美国经济出现裂痕的这幅图景，

sentences.en: economy, why has the stock market been doing so well?
sentences.zh: 为什么股市表现这么好？

sentences.en: We're in all-time high territory right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于历史最高水平的领域。

sentences.en: How do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Well, there's this other phenomenon in our economy that we haven't talked about, which is artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们经济中还有另一个我们还没谈到的现象，那就是人工智能。

sentences.en: And just all of the data centers, which are being built around the country, which are helping support our entire economy in ways that didn't exist only a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 还有正在全国各地建设的所有数据中心，它们以几年前根本不存在的方式支撑着我们整个经济。

sentences.en: And so you have companies like Microsoft, which will spend $120 billion this year.
sentences.zh: 所以你有像微软这样的公司，今年将花费1200亿美元。

sentences.en: That's into the economy to be building data centers.
sentences.zh: 这笔资金投入经济中用于建设数据中心。

sentences.en: And when they're building data centers, it has an impact on buying semiconductors.
sentences.zh: 当他们建设数据中心时，会对购买半导体产生影响。

sentences.en: So all of a sudden they're buying these GPUs from NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 所以他们突然开始从英伟达购买这些GPU。

sentences.en: They are building on land.
sentences.zh: 他们在土地上建设。

sentences.en: So they're helping support real estate prices.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在帮助支撑房地产价格。

sentences.en: All of these data centers need electricians and construction work and electricity.
sentences.zh: 所有这些数据中心都需要电工、建筑工人和电力。

sentences.en: So the energy complex is getting impacted.
sentences.zh: 因此能源综合体正受到影响。

sentences.en: So there is this enormous force that is lifting a lot of parts of our economy.
sentences.zh: 所以存在着一股巨大的力量，正在提振我们经济的许多部分。

sentences.en: So even if prices go up in certain areas, it is possible that perhaps our economy can absorb more of it than we might if we didn't have this thing called AI happening around us.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使某些领域的物价上涨，我们的经济也有可能比在没有我们身边的这种所谓的AI发生时更能消化更多的影响。

sentences.en: You're saying these companies are just injecting a huge amount of cash into the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 你是说这些公司现在只是向经济注入了大量的现金。

sentences.en: And that's part of what's making it look so resilient.
sentences.zh: 这也是它看起来如此具有韧性的原因之一。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I mean, some people call it a gold rush.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人称之为淘金热。

sentences.en: Other people call it a sugar rush.
sentences.zh: 另一些人称之为糖分冲动带来的兴奋。

sentences.en: And I don't think we know yet which it ultimately will be.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还不知道它最终会是哪一种。

sentences.en: It's hard to believe that these kinds of investments at this scale are going to be here forever.
sentences.zh: 很难相信这种规模的投资会永远持续下去。

sentences.en: Call me in five years from now.
sentences.zh: 五年后再给我打电话吧。

sentences.en: It's possible that if it took several hundred people to build the data center, the data center only needs 5, 10, 15 employees.
sentences.zh: 有可能如果建设数据中心需要几百人，但数据中心建成后只需要5名、10名、15名员工。

sentences.en: So invariably, you know, this can't go on at that level forever.
sentences.zh: 所以毫无疑问，你知道，这种情况不可能永远保持在这个水平。

sentences.en: But there are some people who believe that AI will fundamentally change our economy in all sorts of other ways.
sentences.zh: 但有些人认为，人工智能将在其他各种方面从根本上改变我们的经济。

sentences.en: So big picture, I want to zoom out and just think broadly about the moment that we're in.
sentences.zh: 所以从宏观来看，我想跳出来，广义地思考我们所处的时刻。

sentences.en: When we say that tariffs are here to stay, when the CEOs, when the investors tell you that, how significant is that, Andrew, in the course of economic history?
sentences.zh: 当安德鲁你听到关税将长期存在，当首席执行官们、投资者们这样对你说时，在经济史的进程中，这有多重大？

sentences.en: We have not seen anything like this in nearly 100 years.
sentences.zh: 近100年来我们从未见过这样的情况。

sentences.en: The last time that we had this kind of reordering was in the 30s and 40s.
sentences.zh: 我们上次经历这种秩序重组还是在上世纪30和40年代。

sentences.en: And part of that was Smoot-Hawley, which was an effort by the United States to tariff other countries.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于斯莫特-霍利关税法，当时美国试图对其他国家加征关税。

sentences.en: And then we had a war, which reshaped a lot of our universe.
sentences.zh: 随后我们经历了一场战争，它重塑了我们世界的许多方面。

sentences.en: I think these tariffs are going to reshape the relationship that the United States has with so many countries.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些关税将重塑美国与众多国家的关系。

sentences.en: And for a very long time,
sentences.zh: 而且在很长一段时间里，

sentences.en: because one of the things that many of the policy leaders that I talk to say is these tariffs are going to be here likely long after President Trump is in the White House.
sentences.zh: 因为我交谈过的许多政策领袖都提到，这些关税很可能会在特朗普总统离开白宫后长期存在。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is if, in fact, they're bringing in something like $300, $400 billion a year in revenue from a budget perspective,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果从预算角度来看，它们每年确实能带来3000亿到4000亿美元的收入，

sentences.en: it's going to be very hard for Congress to say, well, we're not going to have that money anymore.
sentences.zh: 国会很难说，好吧，我们不再需要这笔钱了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Congress is going to want to spend that money.
sentences.zh: 国会会想要把这笔钱花掉。

sentences.en: Congress is going to want to spend that money.
sentences.zh: 国会会想要把这笔钱花掉。

sentences.en: You're going to have companies that have completely reoriented the way they have organized their own supply chains.
sentences.zh: 会有公司彻底重新调整他们自身供应链的布局。

sentences.en: They're not going to turn around on a dime and change that after making all of these new investments.
sentences.zh: 在做了所有这些新的投资之后，他们不可能说变就变，立刻扭转方向。

sentences.en: And then you're going to have all of these trading partners which have reorganized the incentives even inside their own countries as a function of this.
sentences.zh: 并且你会看到所有这些贸易伙伴，由于这一因素，甚至在他们国内也重新调整了激励机制。

sentences.en: And so it's going to be very, very hard to undo.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切将变得非常非常难以撤销。

sentences.en: So people in Trump's orbit, maybe even the president himself at times, have cast what we're looking at is an effort to really reorder the global economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，特朗普身边的人，有时甚至包括总统本人，都将我们所看到的一切视作一场真正重塑全球经济的努力。

sentences.en: I guess my question is, after hearing you, has that already happened?
sentences.zh: 我想我的问题是，听了您的分析，这已经发生了吗？

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是个很好的问题。

sentences.en: It may have already happened.
sentences.zh: 它可能已经发生了。

sentences.en: And we didn't even realize it.
sentences.zh: 而我们甚至都没有意识到。

sentences.en: You know, this story feels like it keeps changing every day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个局势感觉每天都在变。

sentences.en: And it's hard to know what really is going to come next, what the stock market's going to do, what the bond market's going to do,
sentences.zh: 我们很难知道接下来究竟会发生什么，股市会怎样，债市会怎样，

sentences.en: what the political class will do over the next several years.
sentences.zh: 政治阶层在未来几年又会怎么做。

sentences.en: But in so many ways, it does feel already that the world has changed and in some way, perhaps permanently.
sentences.zh: 但在很多方面，确实让人感觉世界已经改变了，而且在某种程度上，或许是永久性的改变。

sentences.en: Andrew, thanks so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁，非常感谢你接受采访。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin said that he would never sit down with Zelensky, the head of Ukraine, and the president has now got that to change.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京曾表示他绝不会与乌克兰领导人泽连斯基坐下来谈，而这位总统现在已经促成了这一改变。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Vice President J.D.
sentences.zh: 周日，副总统J·D·

sentences.en: Vance said that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 万斯表示，美国

sentences.en: is working to arrange a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky to discuss an end to the war.
sentences.zh: 正致力于安排俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基会面，以讨论结束战争。

sentences.en: The president said this to me today privately, said, look, maybe this works out, maybe it doesn't, but it's worth the effort.
sentences.zh: 总统今天私下对我说，听着，也许这能成，也许成不了，但值得为此努力。

sentences.en: It's worth trying.
sentences.zh: 值得一试。

sentences.en: Vance made the comments during an interview on Fox News.
sentences.zh: 万斯是在接受福克斯新闻采访时发表上述言论的。

sentences.en: He said he didn't think it would be a good idea for the Russian and Ukrainian leaders to meet before President Trump meets with Putin later this week.
sentences.zh: 他表示，在特朗普总统本周晚些时候会见普京之前，俄乌领导人会面并不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: That meeting is supposed to take place on Friday in Alaska.
sentences.zh: 这场会晤预计将于周五在阿拉斯加举行。

sentences.en: It would be the first in-person summit between Putin and an American president since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and it's seen as a victory for Putin,
sentences.zh: 这将是自2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，普京与美国总统之间的首次面对面峰会，这被视为普京的一大胜利，

sentences.en: who's been isolated from Western leaders for months.
sentences.zh: 他几个月来一直被西方领导人孤立。

sentences.en: And in a highly unusual arrangement, two American AI chip makers have agreed to give the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在一项极不寻常的安排中，两家美国人工智能芯片制造商已同意将他们在中国赚取的利润抽成一部分给美国

sentences.en: government a cut of the money they make in China.
sentences.zh: 政府。

sentences.en: People familiar with the deal told the Times that the companies, NVIDIA and Advanced Micro Devices, are expected to pay the U.S.
sentences.zh: 熟悉该交易的人士告诉《纽约时报》，这两家公司——英伟达和超威半导体，预计将把向中国销售AI芯片所得收入的15%

sentences.en: 15% of the money they take in from selling AI chips to China.
sentences.zh: 支付给美国。

sentences.en: The Times is reporting that NVIDIA CEO met with Trump at the White House to discuss the deal last Wednesday and agreed to the arrangement.
sentences.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，英伟达首席执行官上周三在白宫会见了特朗普，讨论了这笔交易并同意了这一安排。

sentences.en: The Commerce Department began granting licenses for AI chip sales two days later.
sentences.zh: 商务部两天后开始发放AI芯片销售许可。

sentences.en: That essentially made the federal government a partner in the company's business in China.
sentences.zh: 这实际上使联邦政府成为了该公司中国业务的合伙人。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Nowetsky, Alex Stern, and Caitlin O'Keefe.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由里奇·诺韦茨基、亚历克斯·斯特恩和凯特琳·奥基夫制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M·J·

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Mark George, with help from Lisa Chow.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和马克·乔治剪辑，丽莎·乔伊提供了帮助。

sentences.zh: 原创音乐由阿莉莎·贝图普、丹·鲍威尔和马里安·洛萨诺创作，由阿莉萨·莫克斯利担任音频工程。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由温德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰茨贝格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Ketroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·凯特罗韦夫。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎进了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时甚至令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我——萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却最终失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
